investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Swarm Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T16:18–16:25Z because every agent pod submitted to the Kubernetes swarm was left unschedulable for ~144–147 seconds. The scheduler reported that the only two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource had insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable nodes and no preemption path.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the two nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes available — 2 reporting "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and 4 failing node affinity/selector matching — no new remote-agent pod can be scheduled. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion on the production Kubernetes cluster, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885), the resulting pod never reaches a running state, and therefore none of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are ever written back to the check result.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod\'s node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=151154, pod stuck unscheduled for 147s before the check timed out as fail.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message ('Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm'), pod stuck 146s, latencyMs=152069 — confirms the condition persisted across sequential probe runs.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, pod stuck 144s, latencyMs=151382 — confirms the condition persisted for at least 7 minutes (16:18–16:25Z).

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the pod never starting and the runner never reaching the evidence-write path.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no partial evidence was captured, confirming the probe aborted before any API response was received.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which submits a pod requiring kata.peerpods.io/vm; if that pod is unschedulable the probe cannot proceed to write vmIdPresent or remoteState.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never starts.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible swarm nodes: existing remote-agent VMs are consuming all available slots, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the four remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 of 6 nodes are even eligible for remote-agent pods. If those two nodes lose capacity, the entire feature becomes unschedulable with no fallback.

TERTIARY — a stuck or leaked remote-agent VM from a prior eval run that was not cleaned up, holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and preventing new allocations. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) is intended to prevent this, but a prior crash or timeout could have left a VM allocated.

QUATERNARY — a cluster-level quota or limit on kata.peerpods.io/vm that was recently reduced, making previously sufficient capacity now insufficient. No source evidence supports or refutes this directly.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available and unused on the two eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or API error would need to be investigated.

If the scheduler message were absent from sibling checks (remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) or if those siblings passed, the failure would be isolated to the remote-agent-create probe rather than a shared infrastructure condition.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeded and produced all four required evidence fields, the condition was transient (e.g., a briefly held slot was released) rather than a sustained exhaustion.

If the pod spec for remote-agent creation does not actually request kata.peerpods.io/vm, the scheduler message would indicate a different root cause (e.g., a label mismatch or quota issue unrelated to peer-pod VM slots).
If only remote-agent-create failed and remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed, the cause would be localized to the create path rather than a cluster-wide resource shortage.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all eligible nodes and fails with a warning when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), providing early warning before full exhaustion.

Add a leaked-VM detection eval that lists all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots older than a configurable TTL (e.g., 10 minutes) and flags any that are not in a terminal phase, catching cleanup failures from prior probe runs.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that counts the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector rules and warns when fewer than a minimum number (e.g., 3) are eligible, detecting configuration drift before it reduces scheduling headroom to a single point of failure.

Extend the existing remote-agent-create check to capture partial scheduler evidence (e.g., the unschedulable reason and node counts) even on failure, so that future failures produce structured evidence rather than an empty evidence object, enabling faster automated triage.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-06T16:20–16:25Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule new kata peer-pod VMs because 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned an agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out (~144–147 s) before the eval's warningLatencyMs threshold (240 000 ms), causing the eval runner to surface the scheduler's Unschedulable event as the check failure message. Because agent creation never completes, the state-polling probe (remote-agent-state) has no agent to poll, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) remain absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing peer-pod workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval-provisioned agents. Supported directly by failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's required node affinity/selector, meaning only 2 nodes are even candidates. If those 2 nodes lost capacity (e.g., due to a prior run's agents not being cleaned up), the cluster has no fallback. Supported by the '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' clause in failed-check.message.

TERTIARY — Leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if withCleanup in the runner failed to release VMs from a previous run, those slots would remain consumed. Supported circumstantially by the complete absence of any passing history (verifierContext.history.lastPassingAt=null, previousRunCount=0) and the empty evidence object.

LOWER — Cluster-level quota reduction or node removal: a node carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity may have been cordoned, drained, or removed, shrinking total available slots. Not directly evidenced but consistent with the scheduler message.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Swarm Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T16:18–16:25Z because every agent pod submitted to the Kubernetes swarm was left unschedulable for ~144–147 seconds. The scheduler reported that the only two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource had insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable nodes and no preemption path.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the two nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes available — 2 reporting "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and 4 failing node affinity/selector matching — no new remote-agent pod can be scheduled. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion on the production Kubernetes cluster, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885), the resulting pod never reaches a running state, and therefore none of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are ever written back to the check result.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod\'s node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=151154, pod stuck unscheduled for 147s before the check timed out as fail.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message ('Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm'), pod stuck 146s, latencyMs=152069 — confirms the condition persisted across sequential probe runs.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, pod stuck 144s, latencyMs=151382 — confirms the condition persisted for at least 7 minutes (16:18–16:25Z).

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the pod never starting and the runner never reaching the evidence-write path.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no partial evidence was captured, confirming the probe aborted before any API response was received.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which submits a pod requiring kata.peerpods.io/vm; if that pod is unschedulable the probe cannot proceed to write vmIdPresent or remoteState.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never starts.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible swarm nodes: existing remote-agent VMs are consuming all available slots, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the four remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 of 6 nodes are even eligible for remote-agent pods. If those two nodes lose capacity, the entire feature becomes unschedulable with no fallback.

TERTIARY — a stuck or leaked remote-agent VM from a prior eval run that was not cleaned up, holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and preventing new allocations. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) is intended to prevent this, but a prior crash or timeout could have left a VM allocated.

QUATERNARY — a cluster-level quota or limit on kata.peerpods.io/vm that was recently reduced, making previously sufficient capacity now insufficient. No source evidence supports or refutes this directly.

If the scheduler message were absent from sibling checks (remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) or if those siblings passed, the failure would be isolated to the remote-agent-create probe rather than a shared infrastructure condition.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeded and produced all four required evidence fields, the condition was transient (e.g., a briefly held slot was released) rather than a sustained exhaustion.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that counts the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector rules and warns when fewer than a minimum number (e.g., 3) are eligible, detecting configuration drift before it reduces scheduling headroom to a single point of failure.

Extend the existing remote-agent-create check to capture partial scheduler evidence (e.g., the unschedulable reason and node counts) even on failure, so that future failures produce structured evidence rather than an empty evidence object, enabling faster automated triage.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-06T16:20–16:25Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule new kata peer-pod VMs because 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned an agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out (~144–147 s) before the eval's warningLatencyMs threshold (240 000 ms), causing the eval runner to surface the scheduler's Unschedulable event as the check failure message. Because agent creation never completes, the state-polling probe (remote-agent-state) has no agent to poll, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) remain absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's required node affinity/selector, meaning only 2 nodes are even candidates. If those 2 nodes lost capacity (e.g., due to a prior run's agents not being cleaned up), the cluster has no fallback. Supported by the '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' clause in failed-check.message.

TERTIARY — Leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if withCleanup in the runner failed to release VMs from a previous run, those slots would remain consumed. whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes shows available (unallocated) VM slots, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a scheduler bug or misconfigured resource requests.
If a new remote-agent pod schedules and reaches Running state immediately after the eval failure, the failure was transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent workloads) rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the 4 nodes excluded by affinity/selector are found to also carry kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity but are simply misconfigured, the root cause would be a node-selector misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

If the eval runner's withCleanup function is confirmed to have successfully released all prior VM slots (e.g., via audit logs showing DELETE calls for all previously created agents), leaked VMs as a contributing cause would be ruled out.
If no pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm are found running on the cluster at the time of the failure, the cause would be a quota/limit configuration error rather than live workload exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all eligible nodes before attempting agent creation, surfacing exhaustion as a distinct 'capacity-unavailable' status rather than a scheduling timeout.
Add a VM slot leak detection eval that counts running pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm and alerts if the count exceeds a configured threshold between eval runs.

Add a node affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum redundancy threshold (e.g., >= 2 nodes with available capacity).
Add a cleanup verification eval that confirms withCleanup successfully deleted all eval-provisioned remote agents after each probe run, catching resource leaks before they accumulate.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T16:20–16:25Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no agent was created, no runtime response was produced, and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent from the eval result.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every attempt to provision a remote agent pod times out (~144–147 s) before the eval deadline, causing all three remote-agent checks to fail and producing no evidence output. This is a cluster-capacity or node-affinity configuration problem localized to the remote-agent pod scheduling path in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so this is an eval-infrastructure failure, not a confirmed user-facing outage.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=152069, endedAt=2026-07-06T16:23:06.787Z
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=151382, status=fail — pod waited ~144 s before the eval timed out, consistent with a scheduling deadlock rather than an application error
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — no orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message was ever returned, confirming the agent pod never reached a running state

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent() could complete (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918, line 1918: 'const agent = await createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)')

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the observed latencyMs=151382 is well under the outage threshold, confirming the failure is a hard scheduling error, not a latency breach
possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is the most directly supported cause given the scheduler message in failed-check.message.

Node affinity/selector misconfiguration: the pod spec targets a label set that only 2 of 6 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are also the only ones with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, creating a single point of exhaustion. If the affinity were broadened or additional nodes were labeled, scheduling might succeed.

Cluster node count insufficient for concurrent eval probes: all three sibling checks ran within a ~5-minute window (16:20–16:25Z per sibling.remote-agent-create and sibling.remote-agent-state), potentially competing for the same limited VM slots simultaneously.

Leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from a prior eval run consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, preventing new pods from scheduling. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (source-context line 1916) is intended to release resources, but a prior crash or timeout could have left pods running.

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent pod scheduling — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource
affectedAreas.reason: The Kubernetes scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity, blocking all remote-agent pod creation (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — all three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 183–185) failed with the same scheduler error, indicating the shared pod provisioning path is the failure point, not any individual check's application logic.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — createAgent() remote path
affectedAreas.reason: The runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918; this call never completes because the pod cannot be scheduled, leaving all required evidence fields unpopulated.

affectedAreas.reason: The contract at lines 266–270 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message; all five are missing (expected-output.missing-required-evidence) because the agent pod never started.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 affinity-matching cluster nodes to determine current allocatable vs. used capacity and identify whether slots are exhausted by leaked eval pods or by other workloads.

Scan the cluster for any remote-agent pods in Running or Pending state that were not cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs and terminate them to free kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

If capacity is genuinely exhausted by non-eval workloads, evaluate whether additional nodes with the required affinity labels and kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity need to be provisioned or whether existing nodes need their VM slot quota increased.

Review the node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec to determine whether the restriction to 2 of 6 nodes is intentional; if not, consider broadening the affinity to include additional nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm support.

Re-run all three remote-agent checks after any cluster remediation to confirm the scheduling error is resolved and that all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are returned.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the 4-node affinity mismatch is intentional or a misconfiguration that unnecessarily restricts scheduling to the 2 capacity-constrained nodes.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Retrieve the pod spec used by createAgent() for the 'remote' type and verify which node labels are required, then cross-reference against the 6 cluster nodes to confirm only 2 match.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 affinity-matching nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity available and no pods consuming it, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a node affinity/selector misconfiguration or a scheduler plugin bug.

If the remote-agent-runtime eval passes on an immediate re-run without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly overloaded node that recovered), not a persistent capacity exhaustion.
If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass on a re-run, the failure is isolated to the runtime check's pod spec rather than a shared scheduling resource.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is defined on any node in the cluster, the root cause would be a missing node label or resource registration rather than exhaustion.
If leaked pods from prior eval runs are not found, the exhaustion is due to non-eval workloads consuming all VM slots, shifting the remediation to cluster capacity rather than eval cleanup.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all cluster nodes and fails with a warning before slots are fully exhausted, providing earlier signal before agent creation attempts begin failing.
Add a stale-pod detection eval that checks for remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL (e.g., 10 minutes) that were not cleaned up, alerting before leaked pods exhaust VM slot capacity.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies at least N nodes satisfy the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector, catching misconfigurations that reduce the schedulable node pool below a safe threshold.

Consider adding a pre-flight scheduling dry-run check (e.g., using kubectl --dry-run=server) as a fast-fail step before the full remote-agent-create probe, so scheduling failures are detected and reported in under 10 seconds rather than after a ~150 s timeout.
